scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY-Inland): Establishment of Back-Yard Mini RAS Unit Gujarat
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India on September 10, 2020. 

This scheme aims to bring about the sustainable development of the fisheries sector in India. 

The PMMSY has a total outlay of ₹20,050 crores for a period of five years from 2020 to 2025. 

The scheme is designed to enhance fish production and productivity in the country. 

One of the key components of PMMSY is the establishment of Back-Yard Mini RAS (Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems) units. 

These units are particularly significant for states like Gujarat, which has a rich tradition of fishing and aquaculture. 

The objective of establishing Back-Yard Mini RAS units is to promote sustainable aquaculture practices. 

The scheme aims to increase fish production by 70 lakh metric tons by 2024-2025. 

It also seeks to create employment opportunities for around 55 lakh people in the fisheries sector. 

The PMMSY focuses on enhancing fish production through various innovative methods. 

The establishment of Mini RAS units is aimed at increasing the income of fish farmers. 

Each Mini RAS unit can produce approximately 10 to 15 tons of fish annually. 

The financial assistance provided under the scheme for setting up a Mini RAS unit is up to 40% of the project cost for individuals. 

For SC/ST and women beneficiaries, the financial assistance can go up to 60% of the project cost. 

The maximum project cost eligible for assistance is ₹20 lakhs. 

This means that an individual can receive financial assistance of up to ₹8 lakhs for a Mini RAS unit. 

The scheme also aims to promote the use of modern technology in aquaculture. 

The Mini RAS units are designed to be environmentally friendly and resource-efficient. 

The objective is to minimize water usage and maximize fish production. 

The eligibility criteria for beneficiaries include being a resident of India. 

Applicants must be at least 18 years of age. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required to apply for the scheme. 

However, applicants must have a basic understanding of fish farming practices. 

The application process involves several steps. 

Interested beneficiaries must first approach the local fisheries department. 

They need to fill out an application form which can be obtained from the fisheries department office. 

Along with the application form, applicants must submit a project report. 

This project report should detail the proposed Mini RAS unit's design and operational plan. 

Applicants must also provide proof of identity and residence. 

Documents such as Aadhar card and bank account details are typically required. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the fisheries department. 

The department may conduct a site visit to assess the feasibility of the proposed unit. 

If approved, the financial assistance will be disbursed in a phased manner. 

The first installment is usually released after the completion of the initial setup. 

Subsequent installments are released based on the progress of the project. 

The PMMSY also emphasizes capacity building and skill development. 

Training programs are organized for beneficiaries to enhance their aquaculture skills. 

These programs are conducted by various fisheries institutes and organizations. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Fisheries under the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

The contact details for the Department of Fisheries can be found on their official website. 

The PMMSY is expected to significantly contribute to the economic development of coastal and inland fishing communities. 

It aims to improve the livelihoods of fishers and fish farmers across the country. 

The scheme also focuses on increasing the availability of high-quality fish seeds. 

This is crucial for enhancing fish production in Mini RAS units. 

The PMMSY is aligned with the government's broader vision of doubling farmers' income. 

The establishment of Mini RAS units is expected to lead to better resource management. 

It promotes the use of renewable energy sources in aquaculture practices. 

The scheme also encourages the adoption of biosecurity measures to prevent disease outbreaks. 

The PMMSY is a part of the larger initiative to promote Blue Revolution in India. 

This initiative aims to increase fish production and productivity in a sustainable manner. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from various stakeholders in the fisheries sector. 

It is seen as a step towards achieving self-sufficiency in fish production. 

The PMMSY also aims to enhance the export potential of Indian fish products. 

This is expected to contribute to the overall growth of the economy. 

The establishment of Mini RAS units is a significant move towards modernizing the fisheries sector. 

It provides an opportunity for small-scale farmers to engage in profitable aquaculture. 

The scheme is expected to have a multiplier effect on the rural economy. 

It will create jobs not only in fish farming but also in allied sectors. 

The PMMSY is a comprehensive approach to address the challenges faced by the fisheries sector. 

It aims to promote sustainable practices while ensuring economic viability. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to improving the livelihoods of fishers. 

The establishment of Back-Yard Mini RAS units in Gujarat is a crucial component of this vision. 

Overall, the PMMSY represents a significant investment in the future of India's fisheries sector. 

It aims to create a robust framework for sustainable aquaculture practices. 

The scheme is expected to have a lasting impact on the socio-economic conditions of fishing communities. 

The PMMSY is a crucial step towards realizing the potential of aquaculture in India. 

It aims to ensure food security and nutritional needs of the population. 

The establishment of Mini RAS units is a forward-thinking approach to aquaculture. 

It aligns with global trends towards sustainable and efficient farming practices. 

The PMMSY is a landmark initiative that will shape the future of fisheries in India.
